newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters reaffirms need for tight fiscal stance.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters reaffirms need for tight fiscal stance.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters, challenged by the opposition over the high level of the New Zealand dollar, on Thursday reaffirmed the government's commitment to a tight fiscal stance.
"There is nothing that assists our exporters and manufacturers more than a government which is committed to keeping expenditure under control," Peters told parliament.

Peters was challenged by Labour finance spokesman Michael Cullen over comments he made after last October's general election (but before becoming Treasurer in December) that New Zealand could not mount an export-led recovery with the currency at such high levels.
Cullen said the New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index had risen three percent since Peters made the comments.
"I think the member overlooks the fact I was not the Treasurer during most of that period," Peters replied.
"I am now, and to paraphrase (former Queensland premier) Joh Bjelke-Petersen, why are you worrying about it when we (the government) are worrying about it?"
In reply to another question over the level of unemployment, Peters said: "It is this government's view we can bring unemployment down further."
He aimed to work with employers, unions and others to achieve that.
Unemployment was 5.9 percent in the December quarter.
